text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak, in a meeting on developing tourism, bans government and public sector firms from building and managing touristic projects on Egypt's coasts. Government to review all policies relating to the development of the Red Sea area. State to promote "conference tourism".
- Mubarak says in ministerial meeting that government must sell its stake in joint-venture firms by the end of 1997 through share issues or private placements.
- Palestinian President Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu to sign the Hebron deal today if the negotiators succeed in wrapping up the details.
- Former U.N. secretary general Boutros-Ghali will return to Egypt on Friday.
- Mubarak says developing Egypt's tourism industry will generate income for the people.
- In a widescale Arab public opinion poll: Mubarak is dubbed the Arab man of the year because of his leading role in the Middle East peace process.
- Former Sudanese prime minister Sadeq el-Mahdi meets Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, says the Sudanese people refuse to live under the current leadership.
- Mubarak says Egypt is reaping the rewards of full-scale development. Red Sea resorts of Hurghada, Sharm el-Sheikh and the Gulf of Suez are a national resource and treasure.
- Sudanese opposition launch serious attacks on Sudan's northeast.
- Man kills wife and daughter and then sets fire to them because he thought his wife was unfaithful.
